text: Scleractinian corals in the Indo-Pacific exhibit physiological thermal plasticity. Under elevated sea surface temperatures exceeding 31 degrees Celsius, Symbiodiniaceae endosymbionts experience photoperiod stress. Host corals upregulate heat-shock proteins (Hsp70 and Hsp90) and antioxidant enzymes including superoxide dismutase and catalase to scavenge free radicals before zooxanthellae detachment occurs. Resilience is notably enhanced in colonies harboring Cladocopium goreaui lineages.
